## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Yudhañcayajātaka* (Ja 460, also referred to as the *Yuvañjaya Jātaka*) is a canonical birth-story preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection [Vetter 1988]. According to the traditional narrative setting, the Buddha related this account while staying at Jetavana in reference to the Great Renunciation (*abhinikkhamana*). In modern scholarship, the Jātaka is cited as an example where an insight into the transience of all conditioned things functions primarily as the direct motive for renouncing worldly life and pursuing ascetic practice [Vetter 1988].

 Automated analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial internal text reuse with the commentary literature, particularly the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Catuttho bhāgo) and the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Across corpora, DharmaNexus detects cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu-avadāna* (with high similarity scores reaching 75) and minor text reuse with the Tibetan *Karmaśataka* (*las brgya tham pa*) [DharmaNexus].
